Acknowledged. Quick triage notes (telco at 08:40 gave us access to traces):

- Symptom: memory allocation failures and worker restarts on nodes serving quantized-v2 model variant. Error logs show repeated "CUDA out of memory" and subsequent 502/504s from the inference proxy.
- Likely trigger: last-night autoscaler policy introduced aggressive vertical scaling to favor denser packing for cost. We hit a regression with quantized kernels at sequence lengths > 512.
- Immediate mitigations applied (08:55):
  * Rolled back autoscaler to conservative profile (pre-2027-10-20).
  * Flipped routing so Catalyst traffic goes to Dedicated GPU pool (reduces heterogeneous packing).
  * Increased node restart backoff to avoid thrashing.
- Observed impact: 09:02 — throughput recovered to ~84% of baseline, 5xx rate declined to 1.7%. Still above target; further tuning required.

Next actions:
- Karthik: run model-level memory profile and if safe, pin quantized-v1 for Catalyst traffic until we patch kernels.
- Lauren: prepare customer-facing timeline + one-sentence status for execs.
- Priya: we need an executive one-pager for Catalyst C-suite by EOD with remediation steps and credits proposal.

Attaching: redwood_playbook_autoscaler.pdf (actioned steps), brief_error_samples.txt

— David Kim
Director, Incident Response — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Catalyst: sudden throughput drop and 5xx spike — immediate help requested

Update from engineering triage:

- Memory heatmap confirms a regression when quantized-v2 kernel uses fused attention path. The kernel falls back to a slower path under certain alignment conditions, increasing peak resident set size and causing allocation failures under high concurrency.
- Short-term action taken (11:45): pinned Catalyst to quantized-v1 and enforced per-instance concurrency limit = 6. This stabilized tail latency.
- Medium-term: we have a patch queued (PR #4321) to change kernel dispatch logic; estimated QA + canary deploy 48 hours with priority testing.

Customer impact & comms:
- Current status for Catalyst: degraded but functional. Checkout and streams experience recovered; we are monitoring fidelity metrics.
- Recommend the following exec message to Catalyst (draft attached): a concise timeline, what we did, user impact, compensation offer (20% credit for 48h window), and next steps including a follow-up dedicated runbook review.

Lauren — can you finalize the customer note and run it by me before we send? Priya — I'll join the executive briefing at 16:00 to review technical details.

— Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Inference Runtime — Redwood Inference

Aaron / Catalyst team —

Thanks again for the rapid collaboration today. Below is a concise summary for execs and customer stakeholders. Please let me know if you want any edits before we ship this to Catalyst's C-suite.

Summary (what happened):
- 07:55 PDT: A recent autoscaler policy + quantized-v2 kernel interaction caused elevated memory usage at high concurrency, leading to repeated OOMs and a throughput decline (~65% drop) with a 5xx spike (~9.8%).

What we did (mitigations):
- 08:55: Rolled autoscaler back to conservative profile.
- 08:55–09:05: Routed Catalyst traffic to Dedicated GPU pool and increased worker backoff to stop restart thrash.
- 11:45: Pinned Catalyst traffic to quantized-v1 and enforced per-instance concurrency limits; tail latency and 5xxs returned near baseline.

Current status (16:40 PDT):
- Throughput: ~95% of baseline for affected routes.
- 5xx rate: stabilized at ~0.6% (within SLO tolerance).
- Fidelity: no evidence of model output regressions from the v1 fallback; we continue to monitor.

Next steps and timeline:
- Engineering will deploy a kernel dispatch patch (PR #4321). QA + staged canary: estimated 48 hours.
- We will run a joint post-mortem and runbook review with Catalyst engineering next week. Proposed time: Mon 10/25 10:00 PDT.
- Compensation: Redwood proposes 20% service credit for the 48-hour incident window; offer pending legal sign-off.

Attachments included: cataly_stderr_tail.log, redwood_playbook_autoscaler.pdf, customer_status_note_v1.md

If acceptable, Lauren will send this to your C-suite and we'll follow with a short executive call for any questions.
